title: Inside an Indian Tiger Reserve: Coexistence is Key to Conservation

researchBrief.angle: Why Coexistence is Key to Conservation
hookIdeas: In a rare glimpse into the lives of India's apex predators, we reveal the shocking truth behind Bengal tigers' river corridor hunts.
As we delve into the heart of a tiger reserve, we uncover the surprising secret to maintaining a delicate balance of species and habitats.
Meet the unsung heroes of conservation: the forest rangers who risk it all to protect India's most majestic wildlife.
talkingPoints: Healthy herds of chital spotted deer and sambar deer play a crucial role in maintaining grassland balance across 400 square kilometers of tropical forest, keeping vegetation under control and preventing soil erosion.
GPS-collared Bengal tigers use river corridors to hunt and patrol territories without encroaching on village farms, ensuring the safety of both humans and wildlife.
Camera-trap grids and acoustic sensors empower wildlife rangers to respond swiftly to poaching threats, reducing human-wildlife conflict and protecting endangered species in real-time.
Protected wildlife corridors have helped wild tiger and deer populations rebound across connected reserves, providing a safe haven for these majestic creatures to thrive.
